# Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform

**Company:** Halden Pay (fictional name; cross-border business payments)
**Location:** Lisbon, Portugal (hybrid, 3 days per week in the office)
**Team:** Data Platform

## The role

Halden Pay is growing quickly, and data sits at the centre of that plan. We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join the Data Platform team. The team builds and runs the shared data platform that analysts, data scientists and product teams rely on, with a focus on reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines.

## Responsibilities

- Own the design, build and day-to-day running of the company's central data platform
- Evaluate and introduce new open-source tools where they bring a clear benefit
- Work with data scientists, analytics engineers and BI colleagues to turn their needs into platform features
- Define and enforce data quality standards, governance rules and access policies

## Tech stack

- Cloud: Google Cloud (BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE)
- Orchestration and transformation: Airflow, dbt
- Engineering: Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, Git

## Requirements

- Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
- Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
- Strong data modelling skills (dimensional modelling; graph modelling is a plus)
- Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud (managed warehouse, serverless compute, containers)
- Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
- Good professional English; Portuguese is a plus

If you meet most but not all of the points above, you are still welcome to apply.

## Benefits

- Base salary plus annual bonus
- Training and certification budget
- Support for open-source contributions
- Hybrid work from a central Lisbon office

Halden Pay is a fintech in the financial services sector, providing business accounts, foreign-exchange risk management and trade finance to exporters. Its culture is commercially driven and client-focused, with friendly colleagues and an emphasis on collaboration, ownership and moving quickly by reducing unnecessary complexity.

The company’s stated values are **Together** (sharing context and supporting colleagues across teams), **Ownership** (taking responsibility, fixing problems and learning from them) and **Pace** (simplifying work to serve clients efficiently). It offers career paths, an annual learning budget and mentoring across departments. Most offices use a hybrid model, typically with three days a week in the office; engineering teams work in product areas including payments, risk, data platform and client experience. Halden Pay has around 40 offices and uses team events and regular get-togethers to build connections. Employee reviews describe a generally friendly, commercially focused environment, while noting that onboarding and training can vary between teams.

Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. I bring hands-on experience with Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Docker, CI/CD and AWS, alongside open-source contributions to an Airflow provider, including a fix and tests merged in two pull requests. I would welcome the opportunity to apply this experience with comparable cloud platforms and contribute to Halden Pay’s evolving data platform.

I would be glad to discuss how I could help Halden Pay build a reliable, reusable platform for its data teams and business. Thank you for your consideration.

Lena Varga-Holm

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. I have nine years of experience building and operating data platforms across e-commerce and payments, with a focus on reusable pipelines, reliable data quality and warehouses that teams can trust. Halden Pay’s emphasis on shared platform capabilities and taking ownership of work that helps clients move efficiently strongly appeals to me.

In my current role at Lukovac Freight Hub, I design, build and operate a production data platform at scale, owning its ingestion layer and approximately 140 Airflow DAGs feeding Snowflake. I migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into more than 420 tested and documented dbt models, reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I have also introduced data contracts with CI checks, built Kafka-based streaming for around 30 million events a day, and replaced full-table extracts with Debezium CDC. The data-contract work established enforceable data-quality standards between product and data teams, reducing broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine per month to two. These projects have involved operating production systems, improving performance and reliability, and making platform changes that benefit teams beyond a single pipeline.

My experience also includes payments data: at Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile roughly 1.2 TB of daily raw transaction files, designed a Redshift cloud data warehouse using dimensional modelling, with more than 30 fact and dimension tables, and added data quality checks for critical finance tables. Across my roles, I have optimised warehouse and transformation workloads through dimensional schema design, incremental processing and platform tuning. The reconciliation engine reduced the finance team’s manual work from around three days to four hours per month-end. I bring hands-on experience with Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Docker, CI/CD and AWS, as well as Snowflake, Redshift and PySpark, alongside open-source contributions to an Airflow provider, including a fix and tests merged in two pull requests. I would welcome the opportunity to apply this experience with comparable cloud platforms and contribute to Halden Pay’s evolving data platform.

I would be glad to discuss how I could help Halden Pay build a reliable, reusable platform for its data teams and business. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional and well-tailored cover letter. It presents relevant senior-level experience, uses credible metrics, connects the candidate's payments background to Halden Pay, and demonstrates ownership of production data platforms. The progression from platform-scale experience to payments data and open-source contribution is logical. The letter is concise and avoids generic personal claims. One minor weakness is that some important requirements—especially advanced Python and SQL, query optimisation on large datasets, and data modelling—are present indirectly rather than being stated in the job ad's exact terms.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly ATS-friendly in plain text: it uses standard paragraphs, no tables or graphics, and includes strong matching terms such as data platform, Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, Kafka, Debezium, Snowflake, Redshift, PySpark, AWS, Docker, CI/CD, data quality and open-source. The explicit job title is also helpful. AI screening probability is high because the document contains quantified, role-relevant evidence rather than only a list of technologies. It could be marginally stronger by explicitly using the supported phrases "dimensional modelling," "query optimisation," "production data platform," and "managed cloud data warehouse." It correctly does not claim Google Cloud experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the core role. It shows experience designing, building and operating a production data platform at scale; large-volume batch and streaming workloads; Airflow and dbt; data quality standards; dimensional modelling; AWS as a comparable cloud environment; professional English; and open-source practice. The payments experience is particularly relevant to Halden Pay's financial-services context. The examples also support the company's Ownership and Pace themes through production ownership, incident reduction, performance improvement and reduced manual work. The candidate's material does not show graph modelling or Portuguese, so these are gaps rather than document defects. Google Cloud itself is not shown, but the AWS experience is a valid comparable-cloud match.
